package.name: Naval Route Tester Trade-Test Validation Patch
package.purpose: Patch the existing 17-region Naval Route Tester based on the first full Hoy trade-route validation run and user-reported blocked-start/path issues.

observations: Initial wind direction was unfavorable for the Hoy; early speeds were materially reduced.
Wind improved substantially by the first TP because global wind direction rotates clockwise over time.
A more direct route toward Kingston with delayed tacking may have been better than making an early detour toward Griffard's Rock.
The route optimizer must compare whole-voyage ETA, not chase the locally favorable wind angle.
A separate Louisbourg -> Griffard's Rock route attempt reported the path/location as blocked.
validation_run.wind_strength_policy: Ignore observed ~23 kt wind intensity. Continue modeling wind direction only.

route_optimizer_patch.objective: Minimize total simulated arrival time, subject to obstacle safety and valid TP transitions.
required_candidate_strategies: Tack-later variants when current poor wind is expected to rotate favorably before a detour pays back
simulation_rules: Advance global wind 6 degrees clockwise per elapsed minute.
Recalculate relative wind and modeled ship speed on every route segment/tack leg.
Do not evaluate the whole voyage with the departure wind angle.
Do not choose a longer detour merely because its initial segment has better wind.
Compare total ETA of candidate strategies through the final destination.
Use a small configurable numerical tolerance to prevent route-flapping when candidate ETAs are effectively tied.

hoy_validation.note: The full-route recording supports the direction-only approach: poor relative wind produced low progress, then speed improved as wind rotated.

blocked_start_and_path_robustness.goal: Eliminate false 'location/path blocked' failures at valid ports, current-position starts, and TP transitions without weakening obstacle safety.

required_fixes.name: Separate semantic port coordinate from navigation water anchor
required_fixes.instruction: A labeled port point may visually sit on dock/shore/land. Keep the semantic port coordinate for UI/economics, but route from/to a dedicated nearest valid navigable-water harbor anchor.

required_fixes.name: Safe snap-to-water
required_fixes.instruction: If a valid start/end point is inside land, raw obstacle, or the normal clearance buffer, search locally for the nearest reachable navigable-water anchor connected to the harbor. Never snap across an island/peninsula or through an obstacle.

required_fixes.name: Port departure/arrival exception
required_fixes.instruction: Apply the existing port-entry/exit clearance exception only inside a small harbor connection zone, then immediately transition back to the normal hard-clearance rules.

required_fixes.name: TP portal robustness
required_fixes.instruction: Treat the full valid TP rectangle/zone as the portal target, not a single possibly blocked center pixel. Search reachable points within the portal zone.

required_fixes.name: Buffered-mask false closure check
required_fixes.instruction: Check whether the derived hard-clearance buffer closes narrow harbor channels or TP approaches that are open in the authoritative raw obstacle mask. Preserve raw-mask truth and use explicit port/TP exceptions rather than globally shrinking safety.

required_fixes.name: Coordinate-transform validation
required_fixes.instruction: Verify world->region and region->world transforms for starts, destinations, and TP exits. A transformed point must land in the intended region/portal and not inside an obstacle because of stitching offsets.

required_fixes.name: Current-position click validation
required_fixes.instruction: If the user clicks actual current position, validate/snap that navigation point independently from the cargo origin. Do not reject the entire trade route because the click is within a few pixels of a shoreline or ship icon.

required_fixes.name: Fallback corridor search
required_fixes.instruction: If one local leg/TP corridor is blocked, automatically try other valid TP corridors before declaring the full route impossible.

diagnostics.player_ui: Normal UI should show a short useful message, not raw debug fields.

automated_regression_tests: For every port, verify a safe path exists from its navigation anchor to at least one reachable local water/TP target where geography permits.
For every port, verify destination arrival can reach its harbor anchor.
For every paired TP zone, verify at least one reachable entry point maps to a valid reachable exit-water point.
Run all-pairs region-level connectivity test over the TP graph.
Run representative port-to-port route tests across every region pair.
Regression: Louisbourg -> Griffard's Rock must not return generic blocked unless a specific local geometry failure is proven.
Regression: Louisbourg -> Port Royal with Hoy and the same departure wind should compare shortest-safe vs immediate-wind vs direct-progress/delayed-tack candidates.
Regression: actual-current-position start just offshore of a port should route successfully.
Regression: a start marker that visually overlaps dock/shore should use harbor water anchor rather than fail.

warnings: Only show blocked-route warning after all valid local snaps/portal points/corridors have been tried.
If a route is possible but wind-poor, show UNFAVORABLE WIND rather than PATH BLOCKED.
If a wind-favored detour is not actually faster end-to-end, do not recommend it.
route_explanation: Show why a non-shortest route was selected: e.g. '2m 14s faster under projected rotating wind.'
If delayed tacking wins, show the planned tack point/time and expected wind direction there.

do_not_change: Do not rebuild or restitch the 17-region world.
Do not replace authoritative raw obstacle masks.
Do not remove hard safety clearance globally.
Do not use random wind speed, storms, gusts, or slow-wind intensity in optimization.
Do not expose internal CONFIRMED/ESTIMATED/PROXY debug labels in the normal player UI.
